O8-04 dental management of a tube-fed person with Parkinson, Alzheimer disease and stroke history. The thickened water and test jelly elsewhere on the page concern a separate herpes pharyngitis case.

O10-02 dysphagia after antipsychotics and Parkinson improved after medication management. O10-03 stage V and recurrent pneumonia resumed one texture-code-4 meal after comprehensive care. A family supplement was unspecified.

O30-02 includes four Parkinson diagnoses among 106 inpatients. Functional Oral Intake Scale results are pooled and the page gives no Parkinson-specific food effect.

One Parkinson case among 22 in a mixed day-service oral function program. Other presentations on this page concern dysphagia position and postoperative oral cancer. No Parkinson-specific food endpoint.

P12-06 stage IV Parkinson with recurrent pneumonia moved from enteral support to purée and then regular oral meals after laryngectomy and recovery from infection. No named food contrast.

P12-09 used crushed thickened instant cup ramen during VF and supervised direct training for one stage III Parkinson patient. Subsequent intake increased during combined care. P12-10 was a separate PSP case.
Two Parkinson diagnoses among 101 people assessed in a psychiatric hospital dysphagia service. No Parkinson-specific swallowing by food.

Continuation describes LSVT LOUD and speech treatment targets in Parkinson's. No exposure to a food, herb, spice, or oil.

Remote dysphagia assessment advised an older woman with Parkinson's and prior pneumonia about textures and feeding support. No specific ingredient comparison.

O19-3 describes five years of oral feeding as diet texture and care needs changed. Water drinking was part of meal rounds. The adjacent jelly case supplies no evidence for the Parkinson participant.
The tardive-dyskinesia report concerns long-term antipsychotics in schizophrenia. Antiparkinsonian drugs are contextual.

P14-7 involved Parkinson syndrome and dementia. Apple juice was one part of a nutritional regimen for pressure ulcers, with no juice-specific swallowing result.

A dental prosthesis was found in the stomach of a patient with Parkinson's. The swallowed object was not food.

P29-1 evaluates family understanding and caregiving after swallowing instruction in a Parkinson case. No named ingredient or ingredient-specific swallowing outcome.
Educational lecture discusses oral transfer in parkinsonism and diet form generically. No test ingredient or outcome.
Symposium characterizes Parkinson and related diseases as gradually progressive dysphagia conditions. No Parkinson food comparison.

SY2-3 and adjacent lecture discuss rehabilitation in Parkinson and related conditions. No disease-specific food challenge reported.

O4-4 describes a gastrostomy decision after aspiration pneumonia and O4-5 describes team care in Parkinson. No named food comparison.

O7-4 describes one patient with Parkinson and MSA history progressing to supervised jelly-shaped food. O7-5 uses MCT in post-stroke nutrition, a separate sample.
O8-3 facility tasting rated potato oyaki and a Peruvian-style simmered tuber dish among recipes. No Parkinson subgroup, measured choking or aspiration.

P31-7 one stage V Parkinson patient had VF aspiration and maintained some oral intake with unnamed jelly and multicomponent therapy. No jelly-specific aspiration reassessment count.
P37-2 seven tube-fed patients with Parkinson comorbidity after stroke, hematoma or disuse. Oral recovery assessed without a named preparation.

O33-1 gastrostomy clinic cohort includes one Parkinson case. Intake function assessed without named foods or Parkinson-specific results.

O55-4 assessed manometry on saliva swallows in 51 Parkinson patients. O55-5 discusses drooling with eyelid spasm in a Parkinson diagnosis with possible PSP. No named intervention food.
P14-3 Parkinson and stroke case with repeated aspiration pneumonia was assessed with KT chart during rehabilitation. No specific causal food or bolus.
P21-1 Parkinson patient with DBS and deconditioning progressed from blended to soft food and regained independent fluids through rehabilitation. No named item or isolated food effect.
P21-2 Parkinson patient with VF penetration/residue continued eating favorite foods such as meats following multidisciplinary home follow-up. No meat species, recipe or event rate reported.

EL2 discusses coordination of breathing and swallowing and cites Parkinson among conditions with disrupted timing. No named clinical food exposure.

EM5-3 discusses Parkinson and MSA in chronic care and identifies worsening intake over time. No named exposure or separate clinical outcome.
O19-5 describes hyoid/larynx mobilization in parkinsonism with old multiple infarcts and another separate stroke case. No diagnosed Parkinson food response.
P11-7 includes an older Parkinson patient whose alertness fell after a medication error and who later regained three oral meals after aspiration pneumonia. No particular food reported.

P12-6 one Parkinson patient managed training-level oral intake with alcoholic-drink jelly prepared by family during rehabilitation. Beverage, alcohol content and bolus-specific airway outcomes unspecified.

Ten staff rated taste and appearance after energy-powder addition to foods including meat-and-potatoes stew, potato salad and coffee. No Parkinson cohort or swallowing outcome.
